scope: KO01 selected actual source records; inventory, not certification

worlds.name: UTol’s sun
worlds.distText: Not on the star chart: position unknown
worlds.blurb: A large red-orange star, bigger than Roshar’s and comparatively close to its inhabited planets. UTol and Komashi orbit it together as a double planet.
worlds.short: Red-orange star of UTol and Komashi.

worlds.name: UTol
worlds.distText: Not on the star chart: position unknown
worlds.blurb: An ocean world with very few landmasses, home to the Sho Del. From Komashi it shines as a pale blue star, the only light that reached through the shroud.

worlds.name: Komashi
worlds.distText: Not on the star chart: position unknown
worlds.blurb: Half of a double planet circling a big red-orange sun, with its twin UTol shining blue in the sky. In one age, Yumi stacks stones to honour the spirits that warm the land. In another, a black shroud hides the sky, nightmares come out of it, and Nikaro paints them away for a living. A spirit binds the two of them together. The habitable land around Kilahito and Torio is only a few hundred miles across; on this globe it is drawn about six times larger so it can be seen.
worlds.short: Stone-stacking and nightmare-painting: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter.

sites.name: Kilahito
sites.desc: A round city in Nagadan laid out in rings and wedges beside a lake, built around a hion line, with the shroud on its west side. Nikaro paints nightmares here.

sites.name: Torio City
sites.desc: The ruined capital of old Torio, west of Kilahito, with red roofs, fountains and dragon statues. The machine that made the shroud was switched on here.

sites.name: The steamwell basin
sites.desc: Warm, humid springs where Yumi’s people lived, heated by the hijo under the ground, with gardens floating in the rising air. Beyond them lie the searing barrens and then the cold wastes.

sites.name: Futinoro
sites.desc: A Nagadan city destroyed by nightmares decades before the story.

sites.name: Jito
sites.desc: A Nagadan city; placed on the coast as a guess.

events.title: Yumi and Nikaro
events.text: A stone-stacker and a nightmare painter are bound together across time and must work out why.

events.title: The shroud lifts
events.text: They destroy the machine behind the shroud, and the sun shines on Komashi again.

record.name: Virtuosity
record.desc: A Shard who splintered herself near Komashi.

record.name: Hoid (Wit)
record.desc: A storyteller who turns up on almost every world under another name, older than he looks.
more: He was on Yolen at the Shattering.
Goes to Scadrial for help after Roshar falls.

record.name: Yumi and Nikaro
record.desc: A spirit-honouring stone-stacker and a nightmare painter.

record.name: Worldhoppers
record.desc: People who cross between worlds, usually through the Cognitive Realm.
more: Silverlight is their crossroads, and its codes set rules for visitors.
By the 2023 books there are starships as well.

sites.name: Kilahito
sites.desc: A round city in Nagadan laid out in rings and wedges beside a lake, built around a hion line, with the shroud on its west side. Nikaro paints nightmares here.

landmarks.name: The shroud’s edge
landmarks.desc: The black shroud along the city’s west side. Painters patrol it at night and paint away the nightmares that come out; at the end Nikaro gathers thirty-seven painters here against an army of them.

landmarks.name: The Noodle Pupil
landmarks.desc: Design’s noodle stand, where Nikaro’s friends gather. Later it becomes the Noodle Princess.

landmarks.name: The hion lines
landmarks.desc: Glowing lines of power that run through the city and light it.

landmarks.name: The carnival
landmarks.desc: Yumi and Nikaro ride the Jotun Line here.

sites.name: Torio City
sites.desc: The ruined capital of old Torio, west of Kilahito, with red roofs, fountains and dragon statues. The machine that made the shroud was switched on here.

landmarks.name: The father machine
landmarks.desc: In Torio City’s grand exhibit hall: the machine switched on at a Festival of Reveals long ago, which consumed the Torish people and made the shroud. Yumi stacks hundreds of stone towers to draw the spirits away until it stops.

sites.name: The steamwell basin
sites.desc: Warm, humid springs where Yumi’s people lived, heated by the hijo under the ground, with gardens floating in the rising air. Beyond them lie the searing barrens and then the cold wastes.

landmarks.name: The place of ritual
landmarks.desc: Where Yumi stacks stones to draw the hijo, once calling a record thirty-seven at a time.

landmarks.name: The orchard shrine
landmarks.desc: The village shrine where Yumi prays each day before her stacking.

sites.name: Futinoro
sites.desc: A Nagadan city destroyed by nightmares decades before the story.

sites.name: Jito
sites.desc: A Nagadan city; placed on the coast as a guess.

events.title: The yoki-hijo
events.text: Yumi spends her days in ritual, stacking stones to call the spirits that warm her people’s land.

events.title: Yumi and Nikaro
events.text: A stone-stacker and a nightmare painter are bound together across time and must work out why.

events.title: The painters’ stand
events.text: Nikaro gathers painters at the edge of the shroud against an army of nightmares, and paints them back into people.

events.title: The shroud lifts
events.text: They destroy the machine behind the shroud, and the sun shines on Komashi again.
